page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core results falling into the bottom 10% tier at 778.19. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6248.71 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8169.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 829.52 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 56.72 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and key-value transactions perform within the middle 50% tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 11.95 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 4977.55.

The primary tradeoff of this server lies in its shared CPU allocation, which contributes to the lower single-core benchmark scores but offers a cost-effective path to acquiring a large 96.0 GB memory footprint. This high resource density makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is suitable for memory-intensive applications, database caching, multi-threaded text and image processing, and lightweight language model inference using small models, whereas medium-to-large model inference is constrained by the CPU architecture and shared resource model.
